items.text: The quintet recorded it over three days in September 2007 at Capitol Studios in Los Angeles.
items.why: Infobox "Recorded: September 19–21, 2007", "Studio: Capitol Studios, Los Angeles"; five players in Personnel.

items.text: 19 to 21 September 2007, Capitol Studios, Los Angeles
The album was a return to hard bop for Roy Hargrove, a style he had long been drawn to.
items.why: "a return to Hargrove's enduring interest in hard bop".

items.text: Before it, he had made several albums that explored jazz within hip-hop and R&B.
items.why: "following several albums in which he explored jazz within a hip-hop and R&B context".

items.text: Hargrove wrote seven of the thirteen tracks, and the rest come from other writers, Sam Cooke among them.
items.why: Track listing: 13 titles, six credited to others (Walton, Marini, Irvine, Willis, Weill and Nash, Cooke), so seven by Hargrove.

items.text: Roy Hargrove and Larry Clothier produced the record, with Jacques Muyal as executive producer.
items.why: Personnel: Clothier and Hargrove producers, "Jacques Muyal - executive producer".

items.text: Al Schmitt recorded and mixed it, and Steve Genewick was the engineer.
items.why: "Al Schmitt - recorded & mixed; Steve Genewick - engineer".

items.text: Hargrove played trumpet and flugelhorn, Justin Robinson played alto saxophone and flute, and Gerald Clayton played piano.
items.why: Personnel: Hargrove trumpet, flugelhorn; Robinson alto saxophone, flute; Clayton piano.

items.text: Danton Boller played bass and Montez Coleman played drums, five players in all.
items.why: "Danton Boller – bass; Montez Coleman – drums"; five musicians listed.

items.text: Cedar Walton wrote it, and it opens the record.
items.why: First in the track list, "( Cedar Walton)".

items.text: Kurt Weill and Ogden Nash wrote it, so it is one of the tunes on the record that Hargrove did not write.
items.why: "'Speak Low' ( Kurt Weill, Ogden Nash)"; not in the "All compositions by Roy Hargrove except as indicated" set.

items.where: listen_for:Bring It On Home To Me
items.text: Sam Cooke wrote it, and it closes the record.
items.why: Last in the track list, "( Sam Cooke)".

missed: The pack's best fact is missing: Strasbourg / St. Denis "has since emerged as a modern-day jazz standard". Also the ballads Joy Is Sorrow Unmasked and Speak Low, which a critic singled out to hear his flugelhorn; the listen_for items say only who wrote each tune.
